pattern.notes: Real exam: two compulsory 3-hour papers (Paper 1 and Paper 2) on the same day, each of 180 marks with about 16–17 questions per subject; the section structure changes from year to year. Recent papers mix four formats in every subject: single-correct MCQs (+3/−1); one-or-more-correct MCQs (+4 if exactly all correct options are chosen, partial +1 per correct option chosen when no wrong option is chosen, −2 otherwise); numerical-answer questions — a non-negative integer or a value to two decimal places, sometimes set in pairs on a common paragraph — with no negative marking; and List-I/List-II matching questions answered by choosing one of four combination codes (+3/−1). This mock: 15 questions per subject drawn from all four formats in 160 minutes, with a uniform scheme of +4 per question, −1 for a wrong single-correct or matching answer and −2 for a wrong multi-correct answer (as in the real paper), multi-correct partial credit of +1 per correct option chosen when no wrong option is chosen, and 0 for a wrong numerical answer.

trendAnalysis.summary: JEE Advanced remains concept-integrating and lengthy; Mathematics and Physics have alternated as the toughest subject (Physics reported toughest in 2026, Mathematics in 2024). Calculus, probability, matrices and vectors/3D dominate Mathematics; mechanics (rotation, fluids), electrostatics/magnetism and modern physics dominate Physics. Chemistry is the most scoring section but physical chemistry numericals and mechanism-based organic questions have grown, while inorganic stays NCERT-anchored (coordination, p-block). Integer-type and matching questions keep guessing low; cut-offs have been around 25–30% of total marks for the common rank list.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the officially released JEE Advanced Paper 1 and Paper 2 question papers and answer keys (IIT Madras 2024, IIT Kanpur 2025, 2026 cycle) as summarised in public analyses (Careers360, Physics Wallah, coaching institute paper reviews), which web search confirmed for chapter emphasis (modern physics, optics, E&M, mechanics; thermodynamics, bonding, coordination; calculus, matrices, probability, vectors/3D). Full paper PDFs could not be fetched, so recurring concept + format + trap patterns were written from the drafter's own knowledge of these papers. Since the 2026 top-up the bank uses the real answer formats — single-correct MCQ, one-or-more-correct MCQ (type msq), numerical answer (integer or two decimals, type numerical; paragraph pairs share a passage) and List-I/List-II matching rendered as one MCQ with four combination codes. The format named in each archetype is the one in which that concept most often appeared in the drafter’s reading of the 2024–2026 papers.

archetypes.pattern: Screw gauge / vernier calliper with positive or negative zero error, often feeding a derived quantity (area, density, resistivity); trap is the sign of the correction
Dimensional analysis of combinations of fundamental constants, dimensions in a new set of base quantities, or error propagation in derived formulae
Projectile or relative-motion condition (velocity perpendicular to initial velocity, river/boat crossing, collision in air)
Two-block system with friction (block on plank, smooth floor), constant or time-varying force: when slipping starts, accelerations of each block
Elastic/inelastic head-on and oblique collisions and successive bounces: velocities, energy fractions, coefficient of restitution
Spinning/sliding ring, disc or sphere placed on a rough surface: final rolling speed via angular momentum about the contact point
Rolling on an incline: accelerations, friction, minimum μ, energy split between translation and rotation for different bodies
Satellites and two-body systems: orbital speed, period, energies, transfer to an elliptical orbit, binary stars

questions.question: A parallel-plate capacitor has capacitance C₀ with air. Over the left half of the plate area, a slab of dielectric constant 3 fills the whole gap; over the right half, a slab of dielectric constant 3 fills half the gap thickness (the rest is air). The new capacitance is
questions.explanation: Left half: 3 × C₀/2 = 3C₀/2. Right half: air and dielectric in series, C = (C₀/2) × 2K/(K + 1) = (C₀/2)(6/4) = 3C₀/4. The halves are in parallel: 3C₀/2 + 3C₀/4 = 9C₀/4.

relevance.note: Mixed side-by-side + stacked dielectrics 9C0/4 – genuine Adv capacitor archetype

questions.question: A screw gauge has a pitch of 0.5 mm and 50 divisions on its circular scale. With the two jaws in contact (no wire), the zero of the main scale is just visible and the circular-scale division coinciding with the reference line is 46. For a wire, two readings are taken: main scale 2 divisions with circular scale 18, and main scale 2 divisions with circular scale 22. The wire is 2.00 m long and its resistance is 0.80 Ω. Using the mean corrected diameter, the resistivity of the material is X × 10⁻⁷ Ω m. Find X (correct to two decimal places; take π = 3.14).
questions.explanation: Least count = 0.5/50 = 0.01 mm. Zero reading 46 means the circular zero has not reached the line: zero error = −(50 − 46)(0.01) = −0.04 mm. Mean observed reading = 2(0.5) + 20(0.01) = 1.20 mm; corrected d = 1.20 − (−0.04) = 1.24 mm. ρ = Rπd²/(4L) = 0.80 × 3.14 × (1.24 × 10⁻³)²/(4 × 2.00) ≈ 4.83 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m. (Wrong sign of correction gives d = 1.16 mm and 4.23.)

questions.question: In a new system of units the base quantities are chosen as force (F), speed (v) and energy (E). Which of the following dimensional relations is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Length = E/F, time = L/v = E/(Fv), mass = E/v² (from E = mv²). Angular momentum = E × time = E²F⁻¹v⁻¹. Surface tension = F/L = F²E⁻¹. Pressure = F/L² = F³E⁻², not F²E⁻¹ (that is surface tension). So (A), (B), (D).

questions.question: Particle A is projected from point O on level ground with speed 20 m/s at an angle θ above the horizontal, where tan θ = 4/3. At the same instant particle B is thrown horizontally towards O with speed 6 m/s from the top of a vertical tower of height h whose foot is 36 m from O, in the plane of A’s motion. The particles collide in mid-air. Take g = 10 m/s². Then
options: h = 48 m and the collision occurs 3 m above the ground
h = 32 m and the collision occurs 3 m above the ground
h = 32 m and the collision occurs 12 m above the ground
h = 24 m and the collision occurs 12 m above the ground
questions.explanation: Both have the same acceleration g, so in B’s frame A moves in a straight line with relative velocity (12 + 6, 16) = (18, 16) m/s. A must head straight at B’s initial position (36, h): h/36 = 16/18 ⇒ h = 32 m, time t = 36/18 = 2 s. Height then = 16(2) − 5(2²) = 12 m (> 0, so the collision is in the air). Ignoring B’s velocity gives h = 48 m.

questions.question: A block of mass 1 kg rests on a plank of mass 4 kg lying on a smooth horizontal floor. The coefficient of friction (static = kinetic) between block and plank is 0.5. A horizontal force F = 2t newton (t in seconds) is applied to the block, starting at t = 0. Take g = 10 m/s². At t = 5 s, the accelerations of the block and the plank are respectively
questions.explanation: Maximum friction on the plank = μmg = 5 N, so the plank’s largest possible acceleration is 5/4 = 1.25 m/s². Common motion needs F = (1 + 4)(1.25) = 6.25 N, reached at t = 3.125 s; after that the block slips. At t = 5 s, F = 10 N: block a = (10 − 5)/1 = 5 m/s², plank a = 5/4 = 1.25 m/s². (2 m/s² each assumes no slipping.)

questions.question: A smooth sphere A moving with speed u collides with an identical sphere B at rest. At the instant of impact the line joining their centres makes 30° with the velocity of A. The coefficient of restitution is 1/2. Which of the following is/are correct?
options: The speed of B after the collision is 3√3u/8
The fraction of the initial kinetic energy lost is 9/32
The velocities of A and B after the collision are perpendicular to each other
The speed of A after the collision is u/2
questions.explanation: Along the line of centres A has u cos30° = (√3/2)u; perpendicular component u/2 is unchanged. Equal masses with e = 1/2: v_A(line) = (1 − e)/2 × (√3/2)u = √3u/8, v_B = (1 + e)/2 × (√3/2)u = 3√3u/8. Speed of A = u√(3/64 + 16/64) = √19u/8 (not u/2). KE fraction left = (19 + 27)/64 = 46/64, so 18/64 = 9/32 is lost. The 90° rule holds only for elastic collisions; here cos(angle) = 3/√57 ≠ 0.

questions.question: A thin ring of mass 2 kg and radius R is launched on a rough horizontal floor with its centre moving at 8 m/s and with a backspin ω₀ such that ω₀R = 2 m/s (the spin alone would roll it backwards). Eventually it rolls without slipping. Find the total heat (in J) produced by friction.
questions.explanation: Friction acts at the contact point, so angular momentum about a fixed point on the floor is conserved: mv₀R − mR²ω₀ = mvR + mR²(v/R) ⇒ v = (v₀ − ω₀R)/2 = 3 m/s (forward). Initial KE = ½(2)(8²) + ½(2)(2²) = 68 J; final KE = ½(2)(3²) + ½(2)(3²) = 18 J. Heat = 50 J.

questions.question:
A uniform solid cylinder of mass 3 kg is released from rest on a rough incline of inclination θ (sin θ = 0.6) and rolls down without slipping. Take g = 10 m/s². List-I gives quantities for this motion and List-II gives their values in SI units.

List-I
(P) Acceleration of the centre of mass
(Q) Friction force acting on the cylinder
(R) Minimum coefficient of static friction needed for rolling
(S) Rotational kinetic energy 2 s after release

List-II
(1) 0.25
(2) 4
(3) 6
(4) 48
(5) 12

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: a = g sin θ/(1 + I/mR²) = 6/1.5 = 4 m/s². Friction f = mg sin θ − ma = 18 − 12 = 6 N (not ma = 12 N). μ_min = f/(mg cos θ) = 6/24 = 0.25. After 2 s it has moved 8 m, so total KE = mg(8)(0.6) = 144 J; for a solid cylinder rotational KE is 1/3 of total = 48 J.

questions.question: A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 2R around a planet of radius R. Its speed is suddenly reduced (direction unchanged) so that the new orbit is an ellipse that just grazes the planet’s surface. By what percentage must the speed be reduced? Give the answer correct to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Apogee r₁ = 2R, perigee r₂ = R. Angular momentum and energy give v_apogee² = 2GMr₂/[r₁(r₁ + r₂)] = GM/(3R). Circular speed at 2R: v₀² = GM/(2R). Ratio v/v₀ = √(2/3) = 0.8165, so the decrease is 18.35 %.

questions.question: Two stars of masses M and 2M, separated by a fixed distance d, revolve in circles about their common centre of mass under mutual gravitation. Which of the following is/are correct?
options: The ratio of kinetic energy of the star of mass M to that of the star of mass 2M is 2
The ratio of angular momentum (about the centre of mass) of the star of mass M to that of the star of mass 2M is 2
The total mechanical energy of the system is −2GM²/d
questions.explanation: Radii: M at 2d/3, 2M at d/3. For M: G(2M)/d² = ω²(2d/3) ⇒ ω² = 3GM/d³ ⇒ T = 2π√(d³/3GM). Same ω: KE ∝ mr² ⇒ M(4/9) : 2M(1/9) = 2; L = mr²ω gives the same ratio 2. Total KE = ½(M(4/9) + 2M(1/9))d²ω² = GM²/d; PE = −2GM²/d; total = −GM²/d, not −2GM²/d.

questions.question: A wide cylindrical tank open at the top has a small hole at its bottom; the area of the hole is 1/400 of the tank’s cross-sectional area. Initially the water stands 1.8 m above the hole. How long (in s) does it take for the water level to fall to one-fourth of its initial height? Take g = 10 m/s².
questions.explanation: A(−dh/dt) = a√(2gh) ⇒ t = (A/a)√(2/g)(√h₁ − √h₂) = 400 × √0.2 × (√1.8 − √0.45) = 400 × √0.2 × √0.45 = 400 × 0.3 = 120 s. (Draining completely would take 240 s; the level falls fastest at the start.)

questions.question: One mole of a monatomic ideal gas is taken through the cycle A → B → C → A. A → B is a straight line on the P–V diagram through the origin, from A(P₀, V₀) to B(2P₀, 2V₀); B → C is isochoric down to pressure P₀; C → A is isobaric. Find the efficiency of the cycle in percent (correct to two decimal places).
questions.explanation: Net work = area of triangle = ½(V₀)(P₀) = P₀V₀/2. Heat enters only along A → B (T rises; B → C and C → A both cool the gas). Q_AB = ΔU + W = (3/2)(4P₀V₀ − P₀V₀) + ½(P₀ + 2P₀)V₀ = 4.5P₀V₀ + 1.5P₀V₀ = 6P₀V₀. Efficiency = 0.5/6 = 1/12 = 8.33 %.

questions.question:
One mole of a monatomic ideal gas undergoes the processes in List-I. List-II gives possible molar heat capacities for the process.

List-I
(P) PV² = constant
(Q) P ∝ V
(R) PV^(5/3) = constant
(S) V ∝ T²

List-II
(1) 0
(2) R/2
(3) 2R
(4) 7R/2
(5) 5R/2

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: For PVⁿ = constant, C = C_V + R/(1 − n) with C_V = 3R/2. PV²: n = 2 ⇒ R/2. P ∝ V: n = −1 ⇒ 2R. Adiabatic (n = 5/3): 0. V ∝ T² with PV = RT gives P ∝ V^(−1/2), n = 1/2 ⇒ 3R/2 + 2R = 7R/2. Writing R/(n − 1) gives the 5R/2 trap.

questions.question: Three rods of the same cross-section meet at a junction J. Rod 1 (conductivity K, length L) has its far end at 100 °C, rod 2 (conductivity 2K, length L) has its far end at 40 °C, and rod 3 (conductivity 3K, length 2L) has its far end at 0 °C. The rods are insulated along their lengths. In the steady state the temperature of J is
questions.explanation: Thermal conductances (in units of KA/L): 1, 2 and 3/2. Zero net heat into J: 1(100 − T) + 2(40 − T) + 1.5(0 − T) = 0 ⇒ 180 = 4.5T ⇒ T = 40 °C. So rod 2 carries no heat. Taking all lengths equal gives 30 °C.

questions.question: A block of mass 1 kg attached to a spring of force constant 100 N/m oscillates on a smooth horizontal floor with amplitude 10 cm. As it passes through the mean position moving to the right, a lump of putty of mass 1 kg moving to the left at 0.5 m/s hits it and sticks. Which of the following is/are correct?
options: The energy of oscillation becomes 1/8 of its initial value
The new time period is 2π/5 s
The maximum speed of the block after the collision is 0.5 m/s
questions.explanation: Before impact v = ωA = 10 × 0.1 = 1 m/s. Momentum: 1(1) − 1(0.5) = 2v′ ⇒ v′ = 0.25 m/s (this is the new maximum speed). New ω′ = √(100/2) = 5√2 rad/s, so T′ = 2π/(5√2) ≈ 0.89 s (not 2π/5). A′ = v′/ω′ = 0.25/(5√2) m = 10/(2√2) cm. Energy: ½(2)(0.25²) = 1/16 J vs ½(100)(0.1²) = 1/2 J ⇒ 1/8.

questions.question: A car moves at 20 m/s towards a large vertical wall, sounding a horn of frequency 500 Hz. A stationary observer stands on the road behind the car (the car is moving away from him). He hears the direct sound and the sound reflected from the wall. Find the beat frequency he hears (in Hz, correct to two decimal places). Speed of sound = 340 m/s; neglect wind.
questions.explanation: Direct sound (source receding): f₁ = 500 × 340/360 = 472.22 Hz. The wall receives f₂ = 500 × 340/320 = 531.25 Hz and, being at rest, reflects it unchanged to the stationary observer. Beats = 531.25 − 472.22 = 59.03 Hz.

questions.question:
Speed of sound in air = 340 m/s. List-I describes vibrating systems and List-II gives frequencies.

List-I
(P) Second harmonic of a pipe 85 cm long, open at both ends
(Q) First overtone of a pipe 85 cm long, closed at one end
(R) Fundamental of a pipe closed at one end, of length 84.0 cm and inner radius 5/3 cm, with end correction 0.6 × radius at the open end
(S) Fourth overtone of a string 50 cm long fixed at both ends, under tension 100 N, with linear mass density 10 g/m

List-II
(1) 100 Hz
(2) 200 Hz
(3) 300 Hz
(4) 400 Hz
(5) 500 Hz

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: Open pipe: f₁ = 340/1.70 = 200 Hz, second harmonic 400 Hz. Closed pipe: f₁ = 340/3.40 = 100 Hz; first overtone is the 3rd harmonic = 300 Hz. End-corrected length 84.0 + 1.0 = 85.0 cm ⇒ 100 Hz. String: v = √(100/0.01) = 100 m/s, f₁ = 100 Hz; fourth overtone = 5th harmonic = 500 Hz.

questions.question: A non-conducting sphere of radius R has volume charge density ρ = ρ₀r/R (0 ≤ r ≤ R), where r is the distance from the centre. Which of the following is/are correct?
options: The electric field at r = R/2 equals the field at r = 2R
The ratio of the potential at the centre to the potential at the surface is 3/2
The magnitude of the electric field is maximum at r = R
questions.explanation: Q(r) = ∫ρ₀(r/R)4πr²dr = πρ₀r⁴/R ⇒ total πρ₀R³. Inside E = ρ₀r²/(4ε₀R) (increasing), outside E = ρ₀R³/(4ε₀r²) (decreasing) ⇒ maximum at R. E(R/2) = ρ₀R/(16ε₀) = E(2R). V(R) = ρ₀R²/(4ε₀); V(0) = V(R) + ∫₀ᴿE dr = ρ₀R²/(4ε₀) + ρ₀R²/(12ε₀) ⇒ ratio 4/3 (3/2 is for a uniform sphere).

questions.question: A parallel-plate air capacitor of capacitance 10 μF is charged to 100 V and disconnected from the battery. A dielectric slab of dielectric constant 4, whose thickness is half the plate separation and whose area equals the plate area, is then pushed fully into the gap. Find the work done by the electric field on the slab (in mJ, correct to two decimal places).
questions.explanation: New capacitance (air d/2 in series with dielectric d/2) = C₀ × 2K/(K + 1) = 16 μF. Charge Q = 1 mC is fixed. U₀ = Q²/2C₀ = 50 mJ, U = Q²/2C = 31.25 mJ. Energy decrease = 18.75 mJ = work done by the field (the slab is pulled in).

questions.question: An ideal 12 V battery is connected in series with a 2 kΩ resistor to a parallel combination of a 4 kΩ resistor and an initially uncharged 3 μF capacitor. The charge on the capacitor 4 ms after the switch is closed is
questions.explanation: Thevenin equivalent across C: E_th = 12 × 4/6 = 8 V, R_th = 2 × 4/6 = 4/3 kΩ. τ = (4/3 kΩ)(3 μF) = 4 ms; final charge = 3 μF × 8 V = 24 μC. q(4 ms) = 24(1 − e⁻¹) μC. Using 12 V gives 36 μC; using only 2 kΩ or 6 kΩ gives the other exponents.

questions.question:
A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance r delivers the same power to an external resistor of 2 Ω as to an external resistor of 8 Ω (each connected alone).

List-I
(P) r (in Ω)
(Q) Maximum power the cell can deliver to an external resistor (in W)
(R) Efficiency of the cell (in %) with the 8 Ω resistor
(S) Current (in A) through the 2 Ω resistor

List-II
(1) 2
(2) 4
(3) 9
(4) 66.7
(5) 33.3

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: E²R₁/(R₁ + r)² = E²R₂/(R₂ + r)² ⇒ r = √(R₁R₂) = 4 Ω. Maximum power when R = r: E²/4r = 144/16 = 9 W. Efficiency = R/(R + r) = 8/12 = 66.7 % (r/(R + r) = 33.3 % is the trap). Current with 2 Ω: 12/6 = 2 A.

questions.question:
Each arrangement in List-I carries a steady current I. List-II gives the magnitude of the magnetic field at the stated point in units of μ₀I/(4πR).

List-I
(P) Centre of a square loop of side 2R
(Q) Centre of a circular loop of radius R
(R) A point at perpendicular distance R from one end of a long (semi-infinite) straight wire, on the perpendicular through that end
(S) Centre of the semicircle of a hairpin-shaped wire: a semicircle of radius R joined to two long parallel straight wires that start at its ends

List-II
(1) 1
(2) 2π
(3) 4√2
(4) π + 2
(5) π

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: Square: each side gives (μ₀I/4πR)(sin45° + sin45°) = √2 units; 4 sides ⇒ 4√2. Circle: μ₀I/2R = 2π units. Semi-infinite wire, point opposite its end: (μ₀I/4πR)(sin90° + sin0°) = 1 unit. Hairpin: semicircle μ₀I/4R = π units plus two semi-infinite wires 1 unit each, all in the same direction ⇒ π + 2.

questions.question: A particle with specific charge q/m = 10⁸ C/kg enters a region where a uniform magnetic field B = 0.2 T and a uniform electric field E = 10⁵ V/m both point along +x. At entry its velocity is (3 × 10⁶ x̂ + 4 × 10⁶ ŷ) m/s. Find the distance (in m, correct to two decimal places) it moves along x during its first two complete revolutions about the x-axis.
questions.explanation: The motion perpendicular to x is uniform circular motion with period T = 2πm/(qB) = 2π/(2 × 10⁷) ≈ 3.14 × 10⁻⁷ s (unaffected by E ∥ B). Along x: a = qE/m = 10¹³ m/s². For t = 2T = 6.283 × 10⁻⁷ s: x = 3 × 10⁶ t + ½(10¹³)t² = 1.885 + 1.974 = 3.86 m.

questions.question: A series LCR circuit with R = 30 Ω, inductive reactance 80 Ω and capacitive reactance 40 Ω (both at 50 Hz) is connected to a 200 V (rms), 50 Hz supply. Which of the following is/are correct?
options: The power factor of the circuit is 0.8
The rms voltage across the inductor is greater than the supply voltage
Resonance would occur at a frequency higher than 50 Hz
questions.explanation: Z = √(30² + 40²) = 50 Ω, I = 4 A, power factor = R/Z = 0.6 (0.8 is sin φ). V_L = 4 × 80 = 320 V > 200 V. X_L > X_C at 50 Hz, so resonance is at a lower frequency: f₀ = 50√(40/80) ≈ 35.4 Hz.

questions.question: A conducting rod of mass 0.1 kg and length 0.5 m slides without friction on two long horizontal parallel rails in a uniform vertical magnetic field of 1 T. The rails are joined at one end through a resistor R in series with an uncharged 0.4 F capacitor. The rod is given an initial speed of 4 m/s. Find the total heat (in mJ) produced in the resistor by the time the current stops.
questions.explanation: Current stops when the capacitor voltage equals BLv. Impulse: m(v₀ − v) = BLq and q = C·BLv ⇒ v = mv₀/(m + CB²L²) = 0.4/0.2 = 2 m/s. Capacitor energy = ½C(BLv)² = ½(0.4)(1)² = 0.2 J. Heat = ½(0.1)(16) − ½(0.1)(4) − 0.2 = 0.8 − 0.2 − 0.2 = 0.4 J = 400 mJ (independent of R).

questions.question: A thin convex lens of focal length 15 cm is placed 45 cm in front of a plane mirror, with its axis normal to the mirror. A small object is placed on the axis 25 cm in front of the lens (on the side away from the mirror). Light passes through the lens, reflects from the mirror and passes through the lens again. The final image is
options: virtual, erect, of the same size, 25 cm from the lens on the object side
real, inverted, 21 cm from the lens on the object side, magnification −0.6
real, erect, 21 cm from the lens on the object side, magnification 0.6
real, erect, 37.5 cm from the lens on the mirror side, magnification 1.5
questions.explanation: First refraction: 1/v = 1/15 − 1/25 ⇒ v = 37.5 cm, m₁ = −1.5. This image is 7.5 cm in front of the mirror; its mirror image is 7.5 cm behind the mirror, i.e. 52.5 cm from the lens (m = +1). Second refraction: object distance 52.5 cm ⇒ 1/v = 1/15 − 1/52.5 ⇒ v = 21 cm on the object side, m₃ = −21/52.5 = −0.4. Total m = (−1.5)(1)(−0.4) = +0.6: real and erect.

questions.question: In a Young’s double-slit experiment with light of wavelength 600 nm, the central point O on the screen is equidistant from the slits. A thin transparent film of refractive index 1.5 is placed over one slit. The minimum thickness of the film for which the intensity at O becomes 3/4 of the maximum intensity of the pattern is
questions.explanation: I = I_max cos²(φ/2). I = 3I_max/4 ⇒ φ/2 = π/6 ⇒ φ = π/3 ⇒ path difference (μ − 1)t = λ/6 ⇒ t = 600/(6 × 0.5) = 200 nm. Taking φ = π/6 (forgetting the half-angle) gives 100 nm.

questions.question: When light of wavelength 248 nm falls on a metal surface the stopping potential is 3.0 V; with light of wavelength 310 nm it is 2.0 V. Take hc = 1240 eV nm and the de Broglie wavelength of an electron of kinetic energy K (in eV) as 1.227/√K nm. Which of the following is/are correct?
options: The work function of the metal is 2.0 eV
Light of wavelength 550 nm cannot eject photoelectrons from this metal
For 248 nm light, the minimum de Broglie wavelength of the emitted photoelectrons is about 0.71 nm
questions.explanation: 248 nm ⇒ 5.0 eV, so φ = 5.0 − 3.0 = 2.0 eV (310 nm: 4.0 − 2.0 = 2.0 eV, consistent). λ₀ = 1240/2 = 620 nm, so 550 nm (2.25 eV) does eject electrons. Fastest electrons have K = 3 eV ⇒ λ_min = 1.227/√3 ≈ 0.71 nm.

questions.question: Based on the paragraph: after how many hours do the activities of A and B become equal?
questions.explanation: A_A = 4A₀·2^(−t), A_B = A₀·2^(−t/2). Equal when 4 = 2^(t/2) ⇒ t = 4 h.

questions.question: Based on the paragraph: after how many hours does the total number of undecayed nuclei (A + B) become one-third of its initial value?
questions.explanation: N = A/λ: N_A0/N_B0 = 4 × λ_B/λ_A = 4 × ½ = 2. Take N_A0 = 2, N_B0 = 1 (total 3). With x = 2^(−t/2): 2x² + x = 1 ⇒ x = ½ ⇒ t = 2 h.

questions.question:
For an electron in the nth Bohr orbit of a hydrogen-like ion of atomic number Z, List-I gives physical quantities and List-II their dependence on n and Z.

List-I
(P) Angular speed of the electron
(Q) Magnetic field at the nucleus due to the orbital motion
(R) Orbital magnetic moment
(S) de Broglie wavelength of the electron

(2) ∝ n (independent of Z)
(3) ∝ Z²/n³
(4) ∝ Z³/n⁵
(5) ∝ Z²/n⁵

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: r ∝ n²/Z, v ∝ Z/n. ω = v/r ∝ Z²/n³. Current I ∝ ω ∝ Z²/n³, so B = μ₀I/2r ∝ Z³/n⁵. Magnetic moment = Iπr² ∝ (Z²/n³)(n⁴/Z²) = n. λ = h/mv ∝ n/Z (equivalently 2πr/n).

questions.question: A solution contains both oxalic acid (H₂C₂O₄) and sodium oxalate (Na₂C₂O₄). A 25.0 mL portion needs 20.0 mL of 0.100 M NaOH for complete neutralisation. Another 25.0 mL portion, acidified with dilute H₂SO₄ and warmed, needs 40.0 mL of 0.0400 M KMnO₄. Find the mass of Na₂C₂O₄ (in g) present per litre of the solution, correct to two decimal places. (Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16)
questions.explanation: Only H₂C₂O₄ reacts with NaOH: n(H₂C₂O₄) = (0.020 × 0.100)/2 = 1.0 mmol. KMnO₄ (n-factor 5) supplies 40 × 0.04 × 5 = 8.0 mmol e⁻; each oxalate gives 2e⁻ ⇒ total oxalate 4.0 mmol. Na₂C₂O₄ = 3.0 mmol per 25 mL ⇒ 0.120 mol/L × 134 g/mol = 16.08 g/L.

questions.question: A sample of Li²⁺ ions, all in the same excited state, emits photons of several energies while returning to the ground state; the most energetic photon has energy 108.8 eV. Take the ground-state energy of the hydrogen atom as −13.6 eV. Which of the following is/are correct?
options: The ions were initially in the n = 3 state
At most three different spectral lines can be emitted
The least energetic photon emitted has energy 17.0 eV
The energy needed to ionise a Li²⁺ ion from that excited state is 40.8 eV
questions.explanation: Eₙ = −13.6 × 9/n² = −122.4/n² eV. Highest photon = 122.4(1 − 1/n²) = 108.8 ⇒ 1/n² = 1/9 ⇒ n = 3. Lines: 3→1, 3→2, 2→1 = 3. Least energetic (3→2): 122.4(1/4 − 1/9) = 17.0 eV. Ionisation from n = 3 needs 122.4/9 = 13.6 eV, not 40.8 eV.

questions.question:

List-I
(P) XeO₂F₂

(5) T-shaped; two lone pairs

questions.explanation: XeO₂F₂: 4 bond pairs + 1 lone pair (trigonal-bipyramidal family) ⇒ see-saw. [ClF₂]⁺: Cl has 6 electrons after the charge, 2 bonds ⇒ 2 lone pairs ⇒ bent. XeOF₄: 5 bonds + 1 lone pair ⇒ square pyramidal. [I₃]⁻: central I has 2 bonds + 3 lone pairs ⇒ linear.

questions.question: According to molecular orbital theory, which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: O₂²⁺ is diamagnetic and has bond order 3
He₂⁺ cannot exist because its bond order is zero
N₂⁺ and N₂⁻ have the same bond order
O₂⁻ has a shorter O–O bond than O₂
questions.explanation: O₂²⁺ has 14 electrons (isoelectronic with N₂): bond order 3, all paired. He₂⁺: (2 − 1)/2 = 0.5, so it can exist. N₂⁺ (13 e⁻) and N₂⁻ (15 e⁻) both have bond order 2.5. O₂⁻ has bond order 1.5 < 2 (O₂), so its bond is longer.

questions.question: A real gas obeys the van der Waals equation with b = 0.040 L mol⁻¹, and its Boyle temperature is 600 K. Using the low-pressure (first order in P) form of the van der Waals equation, its compressibility factor at 300 K and 10 atm is closest to (R = 0.082 L atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: At low pressure Z ≈ 1 + (b − a/RT)P/RT. With T_B = a/(Rb) = 600 K, a/RT = b(T_B/T) = 2b, so Z ≈ 1 − bP/RT = 1 − (0.040 × 10)/(0.082 × 300) = 1 − 0.016 = 0.984. Below T_B attraction dominates, so Z < 1 (1.016 has the sign reversed).

questions.question: One mole of a monatomic ideal gas at 300 K and 10 atm is allowed to expand adiabatically against a constant external pressure of 1 atm until its own pressure becomes 1 atm. Find the final temperature of the gas (in K).
questions.explanation: q = 0 ⇒ ΔU = w: nC_V(T₂ − T₁) = −P_ext(V₂ − V₁) = −(RT₂ − RT₁P_ext/P₁). (3/2)(T₂ − 300) = −(T₂ − 30) ⇒ 2.5T₂ = 480 ⇒ T₂ = 192 K. (The reversible adiabatic formula would wrongly give 300 × 0.1^0.4 ≈ 119 K.)

questions.question:
One mole of a monatomic ideal gas is used in each process of List-I. List-II gives entropy changes.

List-I
(P) ΔS of the surroundings for reversible isothermal expansion from V to 2V
(Q) ΔS of the gas for free expansion into vacuum from V to 2V in an insulated vessel
(R) ΔS of the gas when heated reversibly at constant volume from T to 2T
(S) ΔS of the gas when heated reversibly at constant pressure from T to 2T

List-II
(1) R ln 2
(2) −R ln 2
(3) (3/2)R ln 2
(4) (5/2)R ln 2
(5) zero

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: Reversible isothermal: ΔS_gas = R ln 2 and the surroundings lose the same, −R ln 2. Free expansion: q = 0 but S is a state function, so ΔS_gas = R ln 2 (not zero). Constant V: C_V ln 2 = (3/2)R ln 2. Constant P: C_P ln 2 = (5/2)R ln 2.

questions.question: Based on the paragraph: find the pH of the solution after 25.0 mL of NaOH has been added (correct to two decimal places).
questions.explanation: H₂A = 2.0 mmol, OH⁻ = 2.5 mmol. First 2.0 mmol convert all H₂A to HA⁻; the remaining 0.5 mmol give A²⁻ = 0.5, HA⁻ = 1.5 mmol. Buffer of HA⁻/A²⁻: pH = pKa₂ + log(0.5/1.5) = 7.00 − 0.48 = 6.52.

questions.question: Based on the paragraph: find the pH at the first equivalence point (correct to two decimal places).
questions.explanation: At 20.0 mL all acid is HA⁻, an amphiprotic species: pH = ½(pKa₁ + pKa₂) = ½(3.00 + 7.00) = 5.00 (independent of concentration).

questions.question: For PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g) at a certain temperature, PCl₅ is 50% dissociated when the total equilibrium pressure is 2 atm. At the same temperature, the total pressure at which PCl₅ is 25% dissociated is
questions.explanation: Kp = α²P/(1 − α²) = (0.25 × 2)/0.75 = 2/3 atm. For α = 0.25: P = Kp(1 − α²)/α² = (2/3)(0.9375)/0.0625 = 10 atm. Using α²P/(1 − α) gives 12 atm; neglecting α² in the denominator gives 8 atm.

questions.question: At 298 K, E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = 0.80 V and E°(Cl⁻/AgCl/Ag) = 0.22 V. Taking 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V, find pKsp (= −log Ksp) of AgCl, correct to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: AgCl(s) + e⁻ → Ag + Cl⁻ minus Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag gives AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ with E° = 0.22 − 0.80 = −0.58 V. log Ksp = E°/0.059 = −0.58/0.059 = −9.83 ⇒ pKsp = 9.83.

questions.question: The first-order gas-phase decomposition A(g) → 2B(g) + C(g) is carried out in a closed rigid vessel at constant temperature, starting with pure A at pressure P₀. After 10 min the total pressure is 1.5P₀. Which of the following is/are correct?
options: The rate constant is (1/10) ln(4/3) min⁻¹
The total pressure at t = t½ is 2P₀
The total pressure after 20 min is 2P₀
questions.explanation: If A falls by x, total = P₀ + 2x. 1.5P₀ ⇒ x = 0.25P₀, A left = 0.75P₀ ⇒ k = (1/10) ln(4/3) = 0.0288 min⁻¹, t½ = 0.693/0.0288 ≈ 24.1 min. At t½, x = 0.5P₀ ⇒ total 2P₀. After 20 min A = (0.75)²P₀ = 0.5625P₀, x = 0.4375P₀, total = 1.875P₀ (not 2P₀).

questions.question: The activation energy of a reaction is 80 kJ mol⁻¹. A catalyst lowers it to 60 kJ mol⁻¹ without changing the pre-exponential factor. The catalysed reaction at 300 K has the same rate constant as the uncatalysed reaction at temperature T. Find T (in K).
questions.explanation: k = A e^(−Ea/RT) with the same A ⇒ equal k needs Ea/T equal: 60/300 = 80/T ⇒ T = 400 K.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about hydrolysis is/are correct?
options: Complete hydrolysis of XeF₆ gives XeO₃
NF₃, like NCl₃, is readily hydrolysed by water
Hydrolysis of NCl₃ gives NH₃ and HOCl
Hydrolysis of PCl₃ gives H₃PO₃ and HCl
questions.explanation: XeF₆ + 3H₂O → XeO₃ + 6HF. NCl₃ + 3H₂O → NH₃ + 3HOCl, but NF₃ is not hydrolysed (no vacant orbital on N, strong N–F bonds, F not attacked). PCl₃ + 3H₂O → H₃PO₃ + 3HCl.

questions.question: In the Hall–Héroult process the graphite anodes are consumed by the oxygen liberated at them. If the anode gas is an equimolar mixture of CO and CO₂, find the mass of carbon (in kg) consumed per 27 kg of aluminium produced. (Al = 27, C = 12)
questions.explanation: 27 kg Al = 1 kmol needs 3 kmol electrons. C → CO releases 2e⁻ and C → CO₂ releases 4e⁻. With x kmol of each: 2x + 4x = 3 ⇒ x = 0.5. Carbon = 1.0 kmol = 12 kg. (Only CO₂ would give 9 kg; only CO, 18 kg.)

questions.question: Copper matte (Cu₂S + FeS) is blown with air in a silica-lined Bessemer converter. Which description of the chemistry is correct?
options: Cu₂S is reduced by coke added to the converter, while FeS is removed as FeS₂ slag
Cu₂S is oxidised before FeS, and the iron is later removed from the blister copper by magnetic separation
FeS is oxidised preferentially to FeO, which forms FeSiO₃ slag; then some Cu₂S is oxidised to Cu₂O, which reacts with the remaining Cu₂S to give Cu and SO₂
FeS is removed by froth flotation in the converter, and Cu is obtained by electrolysis of the Cu₂O formed
questions.explanation: Iron has the greater affinity for oxygen, so FeS is oxidised first: 2FeS + 3O₂ → 2FeO + 2SO₂; FeO + SiO₂ → FeSiO₃ (slag). Then 2Cu₂S + 3O₂ → 2Cu₂O + 2SO₂ and 2Cu₂O + Cu₂S → 6Cu + SO₂ (self-reduction), giving blister copper. No coke is needed.

questions.question: Find the total number of unpaired electrons (spin-only picture) in one formula unit each of the following complex ions/molecules taken together: [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻, [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺, [Ni(CO)₄], [NiCl₄]²⁻, [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻, [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺, [Zn(NH₃)₄]²⁺, [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺, [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻.
questions.explanation: [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ d⁵ low spin: 1; [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ d⁶ low spin: 0; [Ni(CO)₄] Ni(0), d¹⁰ after pairing: 0; [NiCl₄]²⁻ tetrahedral d⁸: 2; [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ square planar: 0; [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺ d⁹: 1; [Zn(NH₃)₄]²⁺ d¹⁰: 0; [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺ d³: 3; [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ d⁶ low spin: 0. Total = 7.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about KMnO₄ and K₂Cr₂O₇ is/are correct?
options: In strongly acidic medium KMnO₄ oxidises iodide to iodate
Acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ oxidises H₂S to sulphur
In neutral or faintly alkaline medium MnO₄⁻ is reduced to MnO₂
The conversion of CrO₄²⁻ into Cr₂O₇²⁻ on acidification is a redox reaction
questions.explanation: In acid, MnO₄⁻ oxidises I⁻ only to I₂; iodate forms in neutral/faintly alkaline medium. Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3H₂S + 8H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 3S + 7H₂O. MnO₄⁻ + 2H₂O + 3e⁻ → MnO₂ + 4OH⁻ in neutral/faintly alkaline medium. In 2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ → Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O, chromium stays +6: not redox.

questions.question: Find the total number of stereoisomers of hepta-2,5-dien-4-ol, CH₃–CH=CH–CH(OH)–CH=CH–CH₃.
questions.explanation: Each double bond can be E or Z. If both are the same (E,E or Z,Z), C-4 carries two identical groups and is not a stereocentre: 2 achiral isomers. If they differ (E,Z ≡ Z,E), C-4 has four different groups and the molecule is chiral: 2 enantiomers. Total = 4 (not 2³ = 8).

questions.question: Find the total number of isomers, including stereoisomers, of dimethylcyclohexane.
questions.explanation: 1,1-: 1. 1,2-: cis (meso) + trans (pair of enantiomers) = 3. 1,3-: cis (meso) + trans (pair) = 3. 1,4-: cis and trans, both achiral = 2. Total = 9.

questions.question: Benzene is treated with 1-chloro-2,2-dimethylpropane in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃. The major product is
questions.explanation: The neopentyl chloride–AlCl₃ complex does not alkylate as a primary electrophile; a 1,2-methyl shift gives the tertiary 2-methylbutan-2-yl (tert-pentyl) cation, (CH₃)₂C⁺CH₂CH₃, which attacks benzene to give C₆H₅C(CH₃)₂CH₂CH₃. Neopentylbenzene is the unrearranged trap.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about reactions of but-2-yne is/are correct?
options: Reduction with sodium in liquid ammonia gives trans-but-2-ene
Hydrogenation over Lindlar’s catalyst (Pd/BaSO₄, quinoline) gives cis-but-2-ene
Hydration with dilute H₂SO₄/HgSO₄ gives butanal
questions.explanation: Dissolving-metal reduction gives the trans alkene; Lindlar hydrogenation is syn, giving cis. Hydration gives the enol of a ketone: butan-2-one, not butanal. HBr adds twice; the second Br goes to the carbon already bearing Br (cation stabilised by Br lone pair) ⇒ geminal 2,2-dibromobutane.

questions.question:
List-I gives reactions and List-II gives the product(s) or stereochemical outcome.

(Q) Anisole + HI, heat

(S) Phenol + bromine water

Anisole: I⁻ attacks the methyl carbon (Ar–O bond not cleaved) ⇒ phenol + CH₃I. tert-Butyl methyl ether reacts by SN1 through the stable tert-butyl cation ⇒ (CH₃)₃CI + CH₃OH (not CH₃I). Phenol + Br₂(aq) ⇒ 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

questions.question: Acetophenone is converted by the sequence: (i) I₂/NaOH, then H₃O⁺ → A; (ii) SOCl₂, then NH₃ → B; (iii) Br₂/NaOH, warm → C; (iv) NaNO₂/HCl at 0–5 °C → D; (v) CuCN/KCN → E. Compound E is
questions.explanation: Haloform reaction: C₆H₅COCH₃ → C₆H₅COOH (A) + CHI₃. Acid chloride + NH₃ → benzamide (B). Hofmann bromamide degradation removes one carbon → aniline (C). Diazotisation → benzenediazonium chloride (D); Sandmeyer with CuCN → benzonitrile C₆H₅CN (E). Phenylacetonitrile would keep the extra CH₂.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct?
options: Aniline reacts with bromine water at room temperature to give 2,4,6-tribromoaniline
Direct nitration of aniline with a mixture of conc. HNO₃ and conc. H₂SO₄ gives a substantial amount of m-nitroaniline
Benzenediazonium chloride couples with phenol in mildly alkaline medium to give p-hydroxyazobenzene
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is a convenient method for preparing aniline
questions.explanation: –NH₂ strongly activates the ring, so bromine water gives the tribromo product at once. In strong acid much aniline is protonated to anilinium (meta-directing), so ~47% m-nitroaniline forms. Coupling with phenoxide occurs at the para position (orange dye). Aryl halides do not undergo SN2 with phthalimide anion, so Gabriel synthesis cannot make aniline.

questions.question: Find the number of chiral (stereogenic) carbon atoms in one molecule of sucrose.
questions.explanation: Sucrose = α-D-glucopyranose C-1 linked to β-D-fructofuranose C-2. Glucose unit: C-1 to C-5 are stereocentres (5; C-6 is CH₂OH). Fructose unit: C-2, C-3, C-4 and C-5 (4; C-1 and C-6 are CH₂OH). Total 9.

questions.question:
At 25 °C take pKa(CH₃COOH) = 5.0 and pKb(NH₃) = 5.0. List-I gives aqueous solutions and List-II gives their pH values.

List-I
(P) 0.1 M CH₃COONa
(Q) 0.1 M CH₃COOH
(R) A solution 0.1 M in CH₃COOH and 0.1 M in CH₃COONa
(S) 0.1 M CH₃COONH₄

List-II
(1) 3
(2) 5
(3) 7
(4) 9
(5) 11

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: Salt of weak acid: pH = 7 + ½pKa + ½log C = 7 + 2.5 − 0.5 = 9. Weak acid: pH = ½(pKa − log C) = ½(5 + 1) = 3. Equimolar buffer: pH = pKa = 5. Salt of weak acid and weak base: pH = 7 + ½(pKa − pKb) = 7, independent of concentration.

questions.question: Find the number of one-one functions f : {1, 2, 3, 4} → {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} such that f(i) ≠ i for every i ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4}.
questions.explanation: Inclusion–exclusion over the set of i with f(i) = i: Σ(−1)ᵏ C(4, k) · ⁶⁻ᵏP₄₋ₖ = 360 − 4(60) + 6(12) − 4(3) + 1 = 181.

questions.question: Let z = cos θ + i sin θ with 0 < θ < π, and let w = z/(1 − z²). Which of the following is/are correct?
options: (1 + z)/(1 − z) is a real number
questions.explanation: Since z̄ = 1/z, w = 1/(1/z − z) = 1/(z̄ − z) = 1/(−2i sin θ) = i/(2 sin θ): purely imaginary with modulus 1/(2 sin θ). (1 + z)/(1 − z) = (e^(−iθ/2) + e^(iθ/2))/(e^(−iθ/2) − e^(iθ/2)) = 2cos(θ/2)/(−2i sin(θ/2)) = i cot(θ/2): purely imaginary, not real.

questions.question: Find the number of integers k in the interval [−10, 10] for which both roots of x² − 2kx + k² + k − 5 = 0 are real and less than 5.
questions.explanation: Let f(x) be the quadratic. Need D ≥ 0: 4k² − 4(k² + k − 5) = 4(5 − k) ≥ 0 ⇒ k ≤ 5; vertex k < 5; f(5) > 0: k² − 9k + 20 > 0 ⇒ k < 4 or k > 5. Together k < 4, i.e. k = −10, …, 3: 14 integers. (k = 4 gives roots 3 and 5, which fails.)

questions.question: Let aₖ = 4k − 3 for k ≥ 1. The value of Σₖ₌₁²⁰ 1/(√aₖ + √aₖ₊₁) is
questions.explanation: Rationalise: 1/(√aₖ + √aₖ₊₁) = (√aₖ₊₁ − √aₖ)/(aₖ₊₁ − aₖ) = (√aₖ₊₁ − √aₖ)/4. The sum telescopes to (√a₂₁ − √a₁)/4 = (√81 − 1)/4 = 2.

questions.question: Find the number of ways of distributing 20 identical balls into 4 distinct boxes so that every box gets at least 1 and at most 8 balls.
questions.explanation: Put yᵢ = xᵢ − 1: y₁ + … + y₄ = 16 with 0 ≤ yᵢ ≤ 7. Inclusion–exclusion on yᵢ ≥ 8: C(19, 3) − 4C(11, 3) + 6C(3, 3) = 969 − 660 + 6 = 315.

questions.question: The value of Σᵣ₌₁¹⁰ r · (¹⁰Cᵣ)² is
questions.explanation: r·¹⁰Cᵣ = 10·⁹Cᵣ₋₁, so the sum is 10 Σ ⁹Cᵣ₋₁ ¹⁰C₁₀₋ᵣ = 10 × coefficient of x⁹ in (1 + x)¹⁹ = 10 × ¹⁹C₉ = 10 × 92378 = 923780. (10 × ²⁰C₁₀ = 1847560 forgets the shift; 461890 = 5 × ¹⁹C₉.)

questions.question: Let M be a 3 × 3 real matrix such that M² = I and M ≠ ±I. Which of the following is/are ALWAYS true?
questions.explanation: det(M)² = det(I) = 1. M satisfies x² − 1 = 0, so it is diagonalisable with eigenvalues ±1; not all equal (M ≠ ±I), so the eigenvalues are {1, 1, −1} or {1, −1, −1}: trace = ±1. (I + M)(I − M) = I − M² = O. M need not be symmetric, e.g. M = [[1, 1, 0], [0, −1, 0], [0, 0, 1]].

questions.question: Let A = [[0, 1, 1], [1, 0, 1], [1, 1, 0]] (rows listed). If A⁵ = αA + βI for real numbers α, β, find α + β.
questions.explanation: A has eigenvalues 2, −1, −1 and satisfies A² = A + 2I (minimal polynomial (x − 2)(x + 1)). So λ⁵ = αλ + β for λ = 2 and λ = −1: 32 = 2α + β, −1 = −α + β ⇒ α = 11, β = 10, α + β = 21.

questions.question: Urn U₁ contains 3 white and 2 black balls; urn U₂ contains 1 white and 4 black balls. A fair die is thrown: if it shows 1 or 2, U₁ is chosen, otherwise U₂. Two balls are drawn together from the chosen urn. Which of the following is/are correct?
options: P(U₁ was chosen | both balls are white) = 1
P(one ball is white and one is black) = 7/15
P(U₂ was chosen | one white and one black) = 2/3

questions.question: Two numbers x and y are chosen independently and at random (with replacement) from {1, 2, …, 20}. If p is the probability that x² + y² is divisible by 5, find 100p.
questions.explanation: Squares mod 5: 0 for x ≡ 0 (4 numbers), 1 for x ≡ ±1 (8 numbers), 4 for x ≡ ±2 (8 numbers). x² + y² ≡ 0 needs (0, 0): 16 pairs, or (1, 4)/(4, 1): 2 × 64 = 128 pairs. p = 144/400 = 0.36 ⇒ 100p = 36.

questions.question:
List-I gives equations and List-II gives the number of their solutions in the closed interval [0, 2π].

List-I
(P) sin x + sin 3x = sin 2x
(Q) tan x + sec x = 2 cos x
(R) sin x + cos x = 1 + sin x cos x
(S) cos x + cos 2x + cos 3x = 0

List-II
(1) 2
(2) 3
(3) 4
(4) 6
(5) 7

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: (P) 2 sin 2x cos x = sin 2x ⇒ sin 2x = 0 (0, π/2, π, 3π/2, 2π) or cos x = ½ (π/3, 5π/3): 7. (Q) (1 + sin x)/cos x = 2cos²x/cos x ⇒ 2sin²x + sin x − 1 = 0 ⇒ sin x = ½ (π/6, 5π/6) or −1 (rejected: cos x = 0): 2. (R) t = sin x + cos x: t = 1 + (t² − 1)/2 ⇒ (t − 1)² = 0 ⇒ sin(x + π/4) = 1/√2 ⇒ 0, π/2, 2π: 3. (S) cos 2x(2cos x + 1) = 0 ⇒ π/4, 3π/4, 5π/4, 7π/4, 2π/3, 4π/3: 6.

questions.question: For the circles x² + y² − 4x − 6y + 9 = 0 and x² + y² + 2x + 2y − 7 = 0, the number of common tangents and the equation of the common tangent at their point of contact are
questions.explanation: Centres (2, 3), (−1, −1); radii 2 and 3; distance 5 = sum of radii ⇒ the circles touch externally ⇒ 3 common tangents. The tangent at the contact point is the radical axis S₁ − S₂ = 0: −6x − 8y + 16 = 0 ⇒ 3x + 4y = 8 (it passes through the contact point (4/5, 7/5)).

questions.question: Based on the paragraph: find (P₀Q₀)², the square of the least length of a normal chord.
questions.explanation: With a = 2, the normal at t meets the parabola again at t₂ = −t − 2/t. PQ² = a²(t² − t₂²)² + 4a²(t − t₂)² = 16a²(t² + 1)³/t⁴. d/dt of (t² + 1)³/t⁴ = 0 ⇒ t² = 2 ⇒ PQ² = 16(4)(27/4) = 432 (PQ = 12√3 = 6√3a).

questions.question: Based on the paragraph: if O is the vertex of the parabola, find the area of triangle OP₀Q₀ (correct to two decimal places).
For the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1 with foci S₁ and S₂, and P any point of the ellipse not on the major axis, which of the following is/are correct?
options: The greatest possible area of triangle PS₁S₂ is 12
The tangent at P bisects the angle S₁PS₂ internally
The product of the perpendicular distances from S₁ and S₂ to the tangent at P is 9
questions.explanation: a = 5, b = 3, c = 4. Focal sum = 2a = 10. Area = ½(2c)|y| ≤ ½(8)(3) = 12. The normal (not the tangent) bisects ∠S₁PS₂ internally; the tangent bisects it externally. Product of focal perpendiculars to any tangent = b² = 9.

questions.question: Find the number of points on the real line at which f(x) = |x² − 3|x| + 2| is not differentiable.
questions.explanation: Let g(x) = x² − 3|x| + 2 = (|x| − 1)(|x| − 2). f = |g| has corners where g changes sign: x = ±1, ±2 (4 points). At x = 0, g(0) = 2 > 0 so f = g near 0, and g has the corner of −3|x|: f′(0⁻) = 3, f′(0⁺) = −3. Total 5.

questions.question: For real x ≠ 0, the minimum value of f(x) = x² + 4/x² − 6(x − 2/x) is
questions.explanation: Put t = x − 2/x (t takes every real value). Then x² + 4/x² = t² + 4, so f = t² − 6t + 4 = (t − 3)² − 5 ≥ −5, with equality at t = 3, i.e. x² − 3x − 2 = 0 (real x). AM–GM on x² + 4/x² alone (giving 4) ignores the other term.

questions.question: Find the value of ∫₀^π x sin x/(1 + sin x) dx, correct to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: King’s property (x → π − x, sin unchanged): I = (π/2)∫₀^π sin x/(1 + sin x) dx = (π/2)[π − ∫₀^π dx/(1 + sin x)]. ∫₀^π dx/(1 + sin x) = 2. So I = (π/2)(π − 2) ≈ 1.79.

questions.question: Let R = {(x, y) : 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, 0 ≤ y ≤ min(x², 2 − x)}, and let the line x = α divide R into two parts of equal area. Which of the following is/are correct?
questions.explanation: x² ≤ 2 − x for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1. Area = ∫₀¹x²dx + ∫₁²(2 − x)dx = 1/3 + 1/2 = 5/6. Half = 5/12 > 1/3, so α > 1: 1/3 + (2α − α²/2 − 3/2) = 5/12 ⇒ 6α² − 24α + 19 = 0 ⇒ α = 2 − √30/6 ≈ 1.087. 4α³ = 5 comes from wrongly using x² up to α (its root ≈ 1.077 lies beyond x = 1).

questions.question: Let y(x) satisfy dy/dx = (x + y)² with y(0) = 0. Find y(π/4), correct to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Put v = x + y: dv/dx = 1 + v² ⇒ tan⁻¹v = x + C, v(0) = 0 ⇒ v = tan x. So y = tan x − x and y(π/4) = 1 − π/4 ≈ 0.21.

questions.question: Let y = y(x), x > 0, satisfy dy/dx + y/x = xy² with y(1) = 1. Then y(1/2) equals
questions.explanation: Bernoulli equation: put z = 1/y ⇒ dz/dx − z/x = −x ⇒ d(z/x)/dx = −1 ⇒ z = −x² + Cx. z(1) = 1 ⇒ C = 2, so y = 1/(2x − x²) and y(1/2) = 1/(1 − 1/4) = 4/3.

questions.question: Vectors a, b, c satisfy a + b + c = 0 with |a| = 3, |b| = 4, |c| = 5. Which of the following is/are correct?
options: The cosine of the angle between a and c is −3/5
a × b + b × c + c × a = 0
questions.explanation: |a + b + c|² = 0 ⇒ 50 + 2Σa·b = 0 ⇒ Σa·b = −25. c = −(a + b) ⇒ 25 = 9 + 16 + 2a·b ⇒ a·b = 0 ⇒ |a × b| = 12. a·c = −a·a − a·b = −9 ⇒ cos = −9/15 = −3/5. Crossing a + b + c = 0 with a and b gives a × b = b × c = c × a, so the sum is 3(a × b) ≠ 0.

questions.question:
Let Π be the plane x + 2y + 2z = 9, A the point (1, 1, 1) and L the line (x − 1)/2 = (y − 1)/1 = (z − 1)/2.

List-I
(P) Distance of A from Π
(Q) Distance of Π from the origin
(R) Distance between Π and the plane 2x + 4y + 4z = 3
(S) Sine of the angle between L and Π

List-II
(1) 4/3
(2) 5/2
(3) 8/9
(4) 3
(5) 2

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: |1 + 2 + 2 − 9|/3 = 4/3. Origin: 9/3 = 3. The second plane is x + 2y + 2z = 3/2, so the distance is |9 − 3/2|/3 = 5/2 (not normalising gives 2). sin θ = |(2, 1, 2)·(1, 2, 2)|/(3 × 3) = 8/9.

questions.question: Find lim (n → ∞) Σₖ₌ₙ₊₁³ⁿ 1/√(nk), correct to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: Σ 1/√(nk) = (1/n)Σ 1/√(k/n) for k = n + 1 to 3n, a Riemann sum of ∫₁³ x^(−1/2) dx = 2(√3 − 1) ≈ 1.46.

questions.question:
List-I describes counting problems and List-II gives numbers.

List-I
(P) Number of diagonals of a convex decagon
(Q) Number of triangles whose vertices are vertices of a regular decagon and none of whose sides is a side of the decagon
(R) Number of ways to arrange 5 letters in 5 addressed envelopes so that no letter is in its own envelope
(S) Number of ways to put 6 distinct balls into 3 distinct boxes so that no box is empty

List-II
(1) 35
(2) 44
(3) 50
(4) 540
(5) 60

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: Diagonals: C(10, 2) − 10 = 35. Triangles: C(10, 3) − 10 × 6 (exactly one side) − 10 (two sides) = 50 [= n(n − 4)(n − 5)/6]. Derangements of 5: 44. Onto maps 6 → 3: 3⁶ − 3·2⁶ + 3 = 540. 60 counts triangles with exactly one side common.

questions.question: Let f(x) = x² sin(1/x) for x ≠ 0 and f(0) = 0. Which of the following is/are correct?
options: f is differentiable at x = 0 and f′(0) = 0
f′(x) exists for every real x
questions.explanation: |f(x)| ≤ x² → 0. f′(0) = lim x sin(1/x) = 0. For x ≠ 0, f′(x) = 2x sin(1/x) − cos(1/x), whose limit at 0 does not exist, so f′ is not continuous at 0 even though f′ exists everywhere.

questions.question:
List-I gives functions defined on ℝ and List-II gives the number of points at which each has a local extremum.

List-I
(P) x⁴ − 4x³ + 4x²
(Q) x³ − 3x² + 3x
(R) x^(2/3)(x − 5)
(S) x e^(−x)

List-II
(1) 0
(2) 1
(3) 2
(4) 3
(5) 4

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: (P) x²(x − 2)²: minima at 0, 2 and a maximum at 1 ⇒ 3. (Q) f′ = 3(x − 1)² ≥ 0, no sign change ⇒ 0. (R) f′ = (5/3)x^(−1/3)(x − 2): local maximum at the cusp x = 0 (f′ undefined) and minimum at x = 2 ⇒ 2. (S) f′ = (1 − x)e^(−x): maximum at 1 ⇒ 1.

questions.question:
List-I describes conics and List-II gives eccentricities.

List-I
(P) A hyperbola whose conjugate axis equals half the distance between its foci
(Q) An ellipse whose foci and the ends of whose minor axis are the vertices of a square
(R) The conic 9x² − 16y² = 144
(S) An ellipse whose latus rectum equals half its minor axis

List-II
(1) 2/√3
(2) 1/√2
(3) 5/4
(4) √3/2
(5) 5/3

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: (P) 2b = ae ⇒ b² = a²e²/4 = a²(e² − 1) ⇒ e² = 4/3. (Q) b = ae (square) and b² = a²(1 − e²) ⇒ e² = 1/2. (R) x²/16 − y²/9 = 1 ⇒ e = 5/4 (5/3 belongs to the conjugate hyperbola). (S) 2b²/a = b ⇒ b = a/2 ⇒ e = √3/2.

questions.question:
Two fair six-faced dice are thrown. List-I gives events and List-II their probabilities.

List-I
(P) The larger of the two numbers is 4
(Q) The sum of the numbers is a prime
(R) The product of the numbers is a perfect square
(S) The numbers differ by at most 1

List-II
(1) 7/36
(2) 5/12
(3) 2/9
(4) 4/9
(5) 1/4

Choose the option that matches each entry of List-I with the correct entry of List-II.
questions.explanation: Max = 4: 4² − 3² = 7. Prime sums 2, 3, 5, 7, 11: 1 + 2 + 4 + 6 + 2 = 15 ⇒ 5/12. Square products: six doubles plus (1, 4), (4, 1) = 8 ⇒ 2/9. |difference| ≤ 1: 6 + 10 = 16 ⇒ 4/9.

Let ω = cos(2π/7) + i sin(2π/7). Find the value of (2 − ω)(2 − ω²)(2 − ω³)(2 − ω⁴)(2 − ω⁵)(2 − ω⁶).
questions.explanation: ω, ω², …, ω⁶ are the roots of (x⁷ − 1)/(x − 1) = 1 + x + … + x⁶, so the product equals this polynomial at x = 2: (2⁷ − 1)/(2 − 1) = 127.

passages.text: Consider the parabola y² = 8x and its point P(2t², 4t), t > 0. The normal to the parabola at P meets the parabola again at Q. Among all such normal chords PQ, let P₀Q₀ be the one of least length.
